subjectOf.text: The required review of counterparty history is possible through a platform that creates reputation for both parties and for the smart contract itself, so reputation must attach to code as well as to persons.
subjectOf.abstract: This is possible through a platform that creates reputation for both parties and for the smart contract itself.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Commerce – A Primer on Why Decentralized Reputation Verification Systems Are Needed (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3405401

subjectOf.text: Future decentralized infrastructure products, such as a decentralized verification engine, need to be built to address the inaccuracy of randomly generated information in decentralized systems.
subjectOf.abstract: These are exactly the type of shortcomings future decentralized infrastructure products, such as a decentralized verification engine, need to address.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Preface to (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782191
scope_conditions: decentralized systems with unverified information

subjectOf.text: The correct goal is not to eliminate the middlemen but to automate them, because unlike human middlemen automated middlemen can be designed so that they do not contribute to the corruption they were built to fight.
subjectOf.abstract: Automating these middlemen functions makes them more efficient, like the chemical catalysts in a cell. Unlike human middlemen, automated middlemen can be designed so that they don't contribute to the corruption they were designed to fight.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Future of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782201

subjectOf.text: LER should be built as a bifurcated architecture: voucher-based rewards for equities held in brokerage accounts, and programmable on-chain reward units for tokenized equities.
subjectOf.abstract: LER employs a bifurcated architecture: voucher-based rewards for brokerage-held equities and programmable, on-chain reward units for tokenized equities.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054
scope_conditions: issuer serves both off-chain brokerage holders and on-chain token holders

subjectOf.text: LER can be engineered outside the Howey test by keeping reward units consumptive as discounts or credits, non-yielding, unmarketed for appreciation, and by disabling secondary trading.
subjectOf.abstract: LER could be engineered to fall outside of the Howey test. This is possible by avoiding a reasonable expectation of profits derived from the efforts of others. LER voucher loyalty reward units remain consumptive as discounts/credits, non-yielding, and not marketed for appreciation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054
scope_conditions: United States securities law
secondary trading disabled

subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.

subjectOf.text: Because no standard deviation was known before the runs, the design fixes a masked release in which the analysis releases only each test's variance of paired differences, withholds the mean, and reports the realized power first, and if the realized conjunction power is below 0.80 the substrate is reported as underpowered with the same prominence as any label.

subjectOf.text: The design names a failure pattern in advance: if the likelihood filter, the equal-weight pool, and the reputation pool each carry the negative label against full replacement in every family, the paper issues a registered sentence recording that each had lower capped retention at generation 50 than full replacement, as a registered negative result and not an implementation failure.
